 ### Design Explanation

 1. Function Signature:

    • The function will be named parse_config_file.
    • It will take a single parameter: a string slice (&str) representing the content of the configuration file.
    • It will return a Result<HashMap<String, String>, ConfigError> where ConfigError is a custom error type.
 2. Custom Error Type:

    • We'll define an enum ConfigError that can represent different types of errors that might occur during parsing.
    • This enum will implement both std::fmt::Display and std::error::Error.
 3. Parsing Logic:

    • We'll split the input string into lines using .lines().
    • For each line, we'll skip empty lines and lines that start with #.
    • We'll split each valid line into key-value pairs using .split_once('=').
    • If the split is successful, we'll trim any leading/trailing whitespace from both the key and value before inserting them into the HashMap.
 4. Unit Test:

    • We'll write a unit test to ensure our function works correctly with various inputs, including edge cases.

 ### Implementation

 ▏ rust   copy
 ▏ use std::collections::HashMap;
 ▏ use std::error::Error;
 ▏
 ▏ /// Custom error type for configuration parsing errors.
 ▏ #[derive(Debug)]
 ▏ enum ConfigError {
 ▏     InvalidLine(String),
 ▏ }
 ▏
 ▏ impl std::fmt::Display for ConfigError {
 ▏     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 ▏         match self {
 ▏             ConfigError::InvalidLine(line) => write!(f, "Invalid line: {}", line),
 ▏         }
 ▏     }
 ▏ }
 ▏
 ▏ impl Error for ConfigError {}
 ▏
 ▏ /// Parses a config file of `key = value` lines into a HashMap<String, String>.
 ▏ ///
 ▏ /// Skips blank lines and lines starting with `#`.
 ▏ fn parse_config_file(content: &str) -> Result<HashMap<String, String>, ConfigError> {
 ▏     let mut config_map = HashMap::new();
 ▏
 ▏     for line in content.lines() {
 ▏         if line.trim().is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') {
 ▏             continue; // Skip empty lines and lines starting with '#'
 ▏         }
 ▏
 ▏         let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_once('=').ok_or_else(|| ConfigError::InvalidLine(line.to_string()))?;
 ▏         let key = parts[0].trim().to_string();
 ▏         let value = parts[1].trim().to_string();
 ▏
 ▏         config_map.insert(key, value);
 ▏     }
 ▏
 ▏     Ok(config_map)
 ▏ }
 ▏
 ▏ // Unit test for the parse_config_file function
 ▏ #[cfg(test)]
 ▏ mod tests {
 ▏     use super::*;
 ▏
 ▏     #[test]
 ▏     fn test_parse_config_file() {
 ▏         let config_content = r"
 ▏ # This is a comment
 ▏ key1 = value1
 ▏ key2 = value2
 ▏ key3 = value3
 ▏ ";
 ▏
 ▏         let expected = [
 ▏             ("key1".to_string(), "value1".to_string()),
 ▏             ("key2".to_string(), "value2".to_string()),
 ▏             ("key3".to_string(), "value3".to_string()),
 ▏         ]
 ▏         .iter()
 ▏         .cloned()
 ▏         .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>();
 ▏
 ▏         assert_eq!(parse_config_file(config_content), Ok(expected));
 ▏     }
 ▏
 ▏     #[test]
 ▏     fn test_parse_config_file_with_whitespace() {
 ▏         let config_content = r"
 ▏ key1 = value1
 ▏ key2= value2
 ▏ key3=value3
 ▏ ";
 ▏
 ▏         let expected = [
 ▏             ("key1".to_string(), "value1".to_string()),
 ▏             ("key2".to_string(), "value2".to_string()),
 ▏             ("key3".to_string(), "value3".to_string()),
 ▏         ]
 ▏         .iter()
 ▏         .cloned()
 ▏         .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>();
 ▏
 ▏         assert_eq!(parse_config_file(config_content), Ok(expected));
 ▏     }
 ▏
 ▏     #[test]
 ▏     fn test_parse_config_file_with_invalid_line() {
 ▏         let config_content = r"
 ▏ key1 = value1
 ▏ invalid_line_without_equal_sign
 ▏ key2 = value2
 ▏ ";
 ▏
 ▏         assert_eq!(
 ▏             parse_config_file(config_content),
 ▏             Err(ConfigError::InvalidLine("invalid_line_without_equal_sign".to_string()))
 ▏         );
 ▏     }
 ▏ }

 ### Explanation of the Code

 1. Custom Error Type (ConfigError):

    • This enum represents two possible errors: InvalidLine, which occurs when a line does not contain an equal sign (=).
 2. Implementing Display and Error Traits:

    • These traits allow us to format the error message and convert it into a standard error type.
 3. Function parse_config_file:

    • The function iterates over each line of the input string.
    • It skips empty lines and lines starting with #.
    • It splits each valid line into key-value pairs and trims any extra whitespace.
    • It inserts the key-value pair into the HashMap.
 4. Unit Tests:

    • The tests cover various scenarios, including normal parsing, handling of whitespace, and invalid lines.
    • They use assertions to verify that the function behaves as expected.

 This implementation follows all the provided guidelines, ensuring robustness and maintainability of the code.
